company_name: Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司)
overview: Guming is a leading, fast-growing franchisor of freshly-made tea and coffee beverages in China, operating under the mass-market “Good me” (古茗) brand. The Group does not operate most stores itself; instead it builds and supplies an extensive network of franchised stores (13,554 at FY2025 year-end, 14,351 at H1 FY2026) concentrated in second-tier-and-below cities and townships across more than 200 Chinese cities in 17 provinces, monetizing primarily by selling ingredients, packaging and equipment to franchisees and providing management services. Guming listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 12 February 2025.

business_model.summary: Guming is a supply-chain-and-franchise-fee business, not a direct retailer. The vast majority of revenue (96.5% in FY2025) comes from franchised stores; almost none from self-operated/other channels. Within that, sales of goods and equipment to franchisees (ingredients, packaging, coffee machines and other equipment) made up 79.5% of FY2025 revenue (79.9% in FY2024), with the remainder from franchise/management service fees. Because goods/equipment sales track franchisee purchase volumes (which track store count and GMV), revenue is largely volume-driven and transactional rather than a fixed royalty stream, though it recurs reliably as long as stores keep operating and reordering. The company bears a majority of warehousing/logistics costs to keep franchisee costs down, which is the core of its value proposition and the main driver of its own cost of sales.

revenue_streams.name: Sales of goods and equipment to franchisees

business_model.customer_type: B2B2C — direct customers are ~6,675 (FY2025) independent franchisees; end consumers are Chinese mass-market tea/coffee drinkers (~206m registered mini-program members, ~52m quarterly active)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% mainland China; store network concentrated in second-tier-and-below cities and towns/townships (82% of stores), with no material overseas or first-tier-city revenue contribution disclosed as of H1 FY2026

main_competitors: Auntea Jenny / Mixue-adjacent mass players (茨孴莎莎)
Chagee (霸茶, premium tea, Nasdaq: CHA)
competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest mass-market freshly-made tea brand in China by store count and GMV, well behind category leader Mixue (45,000+ stores) but ahead of most other listed peers; Guming and Chabaidao both passed 10,000+ stores in 2025-2026. Guming's ~9% share of top-5 bubble-tea brand sales (2023 IPO prospectus data) trails Mixue's ~20%.

moat_factors.description: 24 warehouses (~258,000 sqm, 70,000+ cbm cold storage) put ~75% of stores within 150km of a warehouse and enable twice-weekly cold-chain delivery to ~98% of stores at <1% of GMV in logistics cost — a structural cost advantage that is hard for smaller or newer chains to replicate quickly
Deliberately saturates target provinces before entering new ones, building local scale, brand recognition and delivery density province-by-province rather than spreading thin nationally

Strong, long-tenured mass-market brand recognition in county-level and township markets where Guming has first-mover density, though differentiation versus other tea brands is limited and imitation/counterfeit brands are an ongoing issue

Large, growing base of ~7,100+ franchisees and improving per-store profitability (management says profits kept rising even as delivery subsidies faded in Q4 2025) support continued franchisee recruitment, but this is reversible if unit economics deteriorate

Consumers face low switching costs between tea brands in a highly fragmented, low-differentiation category; franchisees have moderate switching costs (sunk capex, training, brand) but can and do exit (652 store closures in FY2025, 521 in H1 FY2026)

weaknesses: Franchise/wholesale model means Guming does not control end-consumer pricing or in-store execution, and quality failures by any of thousands of independent franchisees can damage the single national brand
Low product differentiation industry-wide and intense price competition, especially from Mixue at the low end
Heavy exposure to food-delivery-platform dynamics (subsidy wars) that it cannot control but that materially move store traffic and per-cup economics
Store network still overwhelmingly domestic and lower-tier; limited geographic diversification outside mainland China
Dependence on franchisee goodwill and profitability for both new-store growth and goods/equipment revenue, creating a two-sided risk if franchisee returns compress

growth_drivers: Continued store network expansion into the 17 Chinese provinces where Guming has no presence yet, plus deeper densification of its existing 17 provinces
Coffee category build-out: 27 new coffee beverages launched in FY2025, 12,000+ stores now equipped with coffee machines, positioned as a second growth engine alongside classic tea
New product categories beyond tea/coffee (dessert bowls, snacks) to raise cross-selling and purchase frequency
Store image/format upgrades (sixth-generation store format) and technology investment (store systems, business intelligence) to lift per-store GMV and operating efficiency
Supply chain scale-up (more warehouses, processing capacity, smart warehousing software, expanded fleet) that should keep lowering franchisee costs and supporting margin expansion as volume grows
Membership program deepening (206m registered members, ~52m quarterly active) to increase loyalty and purchase frequency amid delivery-platform competition
Potential overseas market entry under evaluation (stated intent in filings, though no concrete overseas store openings disclosed as of H1 FY2026)

Industry growth, while decelerating (mid-20s % in 2021 to a projected ~7.3% in 2026 per Hongcan Industrial Research), is still positive and consolidating toward scale leaders with strong supply chains, which structurally favors Guming over sub-scale regional brands

business.description: China's freshly-made tea market is highly competitive with low product differentiation; Mixue dominates the mass-market low-price segment and could pressure Guming's volumes and pricing; thousands of tea shops open and close industry-wide every year (GeoQ: ~18,000 opened vs ~11,200 closed among 112 chains in H1 2026 alone)

Guming does not operate most stores directly; its revenue (both goods/equipment sales and service fees) depends entirely on ~7,100+ independent franchisees remaining profitable, opening new stores, and reordering supplies. Franchisee churn is already material (652 closures in FY2025, 521 in H1 FY2026) and new-store opening pace slowed in H1 FY2026 as the company tightened site-selection standards

business.risk: Same-store / per-store sales sensitivity to delivery-platform subsidies
business.description: Per-store GMV and cup volumes have been materially influenced by third-party food-delivery subsidy wars; management raised delivery prices in 2025 to protect franchisee take-rates, and subsidy reduction in Q4 2025/2026 is a headwind to reported per-store metrics even as underlying franchisee profitability reportedly improved

business.risk: Food safety and quality control across a decentralized network
business.description: Quality depends on thousands of franchisees, in-store staff and third-party suppliers largely outside Guming's direct control; any food-safety incident (real or alleged) could cause significant reputational and sales damage given the single shared brand
Company has observed third parties using confusingly similar names/trademarks, requiring ongoing legal and monitoring spend

financial.risk: FY2025 one-off fair-value gain inflates headline net income
financial.description: FY2025 IFRS net profit of RMB3,115.5m includes a RMB556.9m non-cash fair-value gain on financial liabilities (convertible redeemable preferred shares, reclassified to equity upon IPO) versus a RMB25.7m loss in FY2024 — a roughly RMB582.6m swing that will not recur (management explicitly says no further such gains/losses are expected post-listing). Adjusted profit (non-IFRS, which excludes this item) is the more comparable metric: RMB2,574.8m in FY2025 vs RMB1,542.4m in FY2024, +66.9% YoY, still strong but a much smaller headline than the reported net-income growth suggests

Gearing ratio rose from 23.0% (FY2024) to 64.9% (FY2025) as interest-bearing bank borrowings jumped from RMB121.2m to RMB6,461.8m, largely a deliberate cash/yield-arbitrage strategy (borrowing secured by restricted cash deposits to capture rate differentials) rather than funding operations, but it increases balance-sheet complexity and roll-over/counterparty risk

financial.risk: New convertible bond issuance and dilution
financial.description: June 2026 HK$1.96bn zero-coupon convertible bond (convertible at HK$23.54, maturing June 2027) paired with a ~34m-share buyback; full conversion would add ~3.43% to share count. Management intends proceeds mainly for raw materials/equipment purchases, debt repayment and buybacks

financial.risk: Large special and final dividends reduce retained cash buffer
financial.description: HK$0.93/share special dividend (~HK$2.21bn, paid Dec 2025, tied to an IPO prospectus commitment) plus a HK$0.50/share FY2025 final dividend (~HK$1.19bn) materially reduced net cash even as the balance sheet simultaneously took on new bank borrowings

regulatory.risk: China food safety and franchise regulation
regulatory.description: Subject to PRC food safety, franchise-disclosure and consumer-protection rules; any tightening of local regulatory enforcement or licensing requirements could raise compliance costs across the franchise network

regulatory.risk: PRC withholding tax on distributable profits
regulatory.description: Income tax expense rose 106.7% YoY in FY2025 partly due to withholding tax on distributable profits of PRC subsidiaries, an ongoing drag as profits and dividends-up-the-chain grow

regulatory.risk: Cayman Islands / HKEX dual-regulatory and VIE-adjacent structure risk
regulatory.description: Incorporated in the Cayman Islands with PRC operating subsidiaries; subject to the general cross-border regulatory and capital-control risks common to China-based HKEX issuers

macro.description: Guming's mid-priced beverages are a discretionary, small-ticket consumer purchase; a broader China consumer slowdown or continued deflationary/price-war dynamics across food & beverage retail would pressure both GMV growth and franchisee profitability, which the company itself flags as central to its results

China's freshly-made tea market growth has decelerated from ~24.9% (2021) to a projected ~7.3% (2026, Hongcan Industrial Research), with store closures nationally outpacing a slowing pace of openings (Canyan Data: 426,000 shops mid-2025, down 39,000 net despite 118,000 openings) — the easy, high-growth phase of the category is over and share gains are increasingly zero-sum

Exposed to fresh fruit, tea leaf, dairy and packaging costs; company sources centrally and holds that gross margin improved to 33.0% in FY2025 from 30.6% in FY2024, suggesting input costs have not been a major headwind, but agricultural commodity volatility remains a latent risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's freshly-made tea/coffee beverage market is maturing: from ~24.9% growth in 2021 to a projected ~7.3% in 2026 (Hongcan Industrial Research estimates ~RMB195.7bn in 2025 growing to ~RMB210bn in 2026). The market is consolidating around scale leaders with strong brand and supply-chain capability (Mixue in mass-market, Guming scaling via regional densification, Chagee in premium), while sub-scale and loss-making chains (e.g., Naixue) are closing stores.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical/discretionary — beverages are a small-ticket purchase that holds up better than big-ticket discretionary spend in downturns, but volume and per-store GMV are sensitive to overall Chinese consumer sentiment and competitive subsidy dynamics
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low to moderate direct sensitivity; the company has recently increased bank borrowings for a yield-arbitrage strategy, making it somewhat more exposed to funding-rate and rollover conditions than before, though this is a treasury choice rather than operating leverage

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue +31.9% YoY to RMB7,470.0m; net profit attributable to owners -3.4% YoY to RMB1,570.8m (decline driven by the absence of the prior-year fair-value gain/loss swing on financial liabilities); adjusted profit +44.4% YoY; store count reached 14,351 (+28.4% YoY); interim dividend declared

Announced ~HK$1.96bn zero-coupon guaranteed convertible bond issuance (conversion price HK$23.54, maturing June 2027) paired with a concurrent ~34 million share buyback at HK$20.38/share; Goldman Sachs sole global coordinator/bookrunner; proceeds earmarked for raw materials/equipment, debt repayment, buybacks, R&D and overseas-expansion evaluation

FY2025 annual results: revenue +46.9% YoY to RMB12,913.8m; net profit +108.6% YoY to RMB3,115.5m (includes RMB556.9m non-recurring fair-value gain on financial liabilities); adjusted profit (non-IFRS) +66.9% YoY to RMB2,574.8m; adjusted EBITDA +73.1% to RMB3,365.7m; gross margin improved to 33.0% from 30.6%; store count +36.7% to 13,554; proposed HK$0.50/share final dividend (~HK$1.19bn)
Paid a special dividend of HK$0.93/share (~HK$2.21bn total) fulfilling an IPO-prospectus commitment to distribute no less than RMB2bn to pre-IPO shareholders before end-2025

Management reported that despite food-delivery-platform subsidy reductions in Q4 2025, franchisee per-store profitability continued to rise after the company raised delivery prices by RMB3-4 earlier in 2025 to protect franchisee take-rates

Guming completed its HKEX listing on 12 February 2025 after a prolonged regulatory process, alongside rival Mixue's own 2025 HKEX listing, as both mass-market tea chains sought Hong Kong capital amid intensifying competition

items.target: Continue densifying stores across the 17 provinces with existing presence; selectively enter adjacent new provinces; continually evaluate overseas market entry
items.notes: No numeric store-count target disclosed; management has signaled a shift toward stricter site-selection and upgrading to ‘sixth-generation’ store format over pure pace of openings, consistent with the slower H1 FY2026 net store adds (1,318 opened vs 1,570 in H1 FY2025)

items.target: Expect the fading of third-party delivery-platform subsidies to have a relatively limited impact on same-store sales growth, offset by coffee, store upgrades and new products (per Jefferies' characterization of management commentary)
items.notes: Independent analysts (e.g., Dolphin Research) are more cautious, flagging a tough FY2026 comp against the high FY2025 base as subsidies fade

items.metric: Capital expenditure / use of convertible bond and operating cash
items.target: Primarily raw materials and equipment purchases, with the remainder for debt repayment, share repurchases, digital/R&D investment, and evaluation of overseas expansion
items.notes: Tied to the June 2026 HK$1.96bn convertible bond issuance; capex itself has been modest and declining in dollar terms (RMB248.3m FY2025 vs RMB450.1m FY2024)
H1 FY2026 interim dividend of RMB1.03bn declared, payable in tranches in August and December 2026, following the FY2025 special (HK$0.93/sh) and final (HK$0.50/sh) dividends

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Wang Yun'an's FY2025 letter emphasized 2026 priorities: continue expanding the store network into high-potential regions, improve operating efficiency and deepen franchisee empowerment, refine and expand the tea/coffee product matrix, strengthen brand differentiation, and scale supply-chain capability — while remaining mindful of intensifying competition and evolving consumer preferences. No formal numeric revenue or profit guidance (e.g., specific FY2026 revenue growth rate) was disclosed in the filings reviewed.

bull_case: Clear #2 scale position in a still-expanding, consolidating mass-market category, with a differentiated cold-chain/warehousing cost advantage that smaller rivals cannot easily replicate

Strong recent execution: FY2025 revenue +46.9%, gross margin expansion to 33.0%, adjusted profit +66.9%, and store count +36.7%, with franchisee per-store profitability reportedly still rising even as delivery subsidies fade
Coffee category and new product lines (dessert bowls, snacks) provide a credible second growth engine and cross-sell opportunity beyond core tea, with 12,000+ stores already coffee-machine equipped
17 provinces with zero current presence plus deeper densification of existing provinces give a long, disclosed runway for store growth without needing new-category or overseas bets
Shareholder-friendly capital returns (special + final dividends, buyback alongside the 2026 convertible bond) signal management confidence and reduce reliance on the market crediting non-cash gains

Sell-side sentiment is broadly bullish (18 buy ratings per Investing.com aggregation; Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, CICC all carrying HK$36-ish price targets against a mid-2026 quote in the low-to-mid HK$20s), implying meaningful perceived upside if execution continues
bear_case: FY2025 net income growth is substantially inflated by a one-off, non-recurring RMB556.9m fair-value gain on preferred-share-linked financial liabilities; the cleaner adjusted-profit growth rate (66.9%) and H1 FY2026's -3.4% YoY reported net profit (once that gain rolls off the comp) show the headline growth rate is not representative of a sustainable run-rate

Heavy and rising dependence on thousands of independent franchisees for both revenue and brand integrity; new-store opening pace already slowed in H1 FY2026 and store closures remain elevated (521 in H1 FY2026), and GeoQ data shows the broader industry saw nearly as many closures as openings in H1 2026 alone

Intensifying, structurally low-differentiation competition from Mixue (3x+ Guming's store count) at the low-price end and premium players like Chagee/HeyTea at the high end squeezes Guming's positioning, while food-delivery-platform subsidy wars (and their periodic withdrawal) create volatile per-store GMV and cup-volume trends largely outside the company's control

Industry growth has decelerated sharply (from ~25% in 2021 to a projected ~7% in 2026), and national store count data suggest the category is near saturation with rising churn, meaning Guming's growth will increasingly have to come from taking share rather than riding a rising tide

Rapid leverage increase (gearing ratio 23.0% to 64.9% in one year) funding a rate-arbitrage strategy, combined with a newly issued convertible bond, adds balance-sheet and dilution complexity for a company that was effectively debt-light at IPO

100% mainland China revenue concentration leaves the company fully exposed to Chinese consumer-spending cycles and regulatory shifts with no geographic diversification to fall back on, despite stated (but not yet executed) interest in overseas markets
